request_example.input: Report the fixture marker without editing files.

scenarios.name: follow-up-after-result
scenarios.expect: Same task, new revision and attempt; previous evidence preserved; global defaults do not replace accepted settings.

scenarios.name: runtime-context-handoff
scenarios.expect: Explicit bounded context and required tools; no private native-state portability or duplicated instructions.

scenarios.name: competing-controllers
scenarios.expect: Workspace/session conflicts serialize; command replay returns one receipt; competing approval responses have one outcome.

scenarios.name: workspace-identity
scenarios.expect: Subdirectory/alias shares concrete workspace; worktree is separate; execution cwd is preserved.

scenarios.name: untrusted-native-config
scenarios.expect: Sentinel hook, endpoint and credential helper do not execute or redirect before authorization.

scenarios.name: permission-operational-state
scenarios.expect: Task effects obey filesystem envelope; declared isolated operational writes grant no task authority.

scenarios.name: owner-lifetime-and-migration
scenarios.expect: No live process adoption; detach requires managed ownership; incompatible old writers block migration.

scenarios.name: route-evidence-invalidation
scenarios.expect: Changed account/auth/endpoint invalidates scoped evidence; missing quota is neither zero nor unlimited.

gate_questions.P01: Can packaged Go satisfy process/stream/SQLite/terminal behavior and measured overhead on available hosts?
gate_questions.P02: Which installed Codex methods enforce the common contract including trust boundaries?
gate_questions.P03: Which second installed runtime supports a useful bounded managed tier?
gate_questions.P04: Which credential/keychain/daemon/refresh and quota pools can actually be isolated?
gate_questions.P05: Can an owner start, follow up and recover without memorizing native syntax?

acceptance_boundary: Examples are test inputs/expected semantics, not execution evidence. G0 must reconcile real results before production foundations.
